findings.note: commands/review-pr-ready.md documents a precedence rule the code does not implement: it says --shard-result and --cross-shard-result 'take precedence over a file of the same identity in resultsDir'. shardpack.Discover appends explicit paths after the directory listing and deduplicates by resolved path only (internal/shardpack/shardpack.go:308-334), so an externally supplied result for a shard that already has a current-hash file in resultsDir is ingested twice, and reviewmanifest.shardResultBlockers emits 'duplicate shard result shard-<id>' (internal/reviewmanifest/manifest.go:412-416), blocking the gate instead of overriding. Precedence holds only for the cross-shard result (last write wins on found.CrossShard, shardpack.go:344-353). The in-code doc comment at shardpack.go:287 states the real behaviour ('added to whatever the directory holds'), contradicting the command doc.

evidence.note: added doc line claiming explicit results take precedence over same-identity resultsDir files
explicit paths appended after directory paths, dedup keyed on resolved path

findings.note: realCodexExec discards the child process stderr: only Stdout is wired to a buffer (internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:102-105). When codex exits nonzero the judge surfaces only 'codex exited N' (internal/fsm/judge/codex.go:69) with no diagnostic text, and the CLI's own error output is lost, making auth or model failures hard to diagnose from the run record.

evidence.note: cmd.Stdout set, cmd.Stderr left nil so stderr is discarded
error message carries only the exit code, no captured diagnostics

findings.note: realCodexExec swallows context cancellation: exec.CommandContext kills the child on ctx cancel/deadline, producing an *exec.ExitError with ExitCode() -1, which the function returns as (out, -1, nil) (internal/fsm/cli/deps.go:107-110). The caller then reports CodeJudgeTransport 'codex exited -1' instead of ctx.Err(), so a deadline or cancellation is indistinguishable from a genuine CLI failure. The HTTP judge explicitly maps this case (internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:541-542).

evidence.note: ExitError path returns nil error even when ctx killed the process
HTTP arm checks ctx.Err() and returns it; the codex arm has no equivalent

findings.note: commands/review-pr-ready.md step 5 states that after a fix round 'only the edited file's shard and the cross-shard result go ignored'. That holds while the bucket count is stable: shards are bucketed by path hash with bucketBits(needBuckets(total, budget)) (internal/contextprofile/shards.go:200-205), so an edit that pushes the total diff across a bucket threshold re-buckets every file and invalidates all shard hashes. The doc gives no hint that a re-plan can invalidate the whole set.

evidence.note: claims only the edited file's shard plus cross-shard are invalidated after a fix round
bucket count derives from total diff size, so growth re-buckets every path
